subject: Post-call: Veridian latency targets & engineering handoff
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Pritchard <alex@veridian.ai>; SRE Team <sre@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Veridian latency targets & engineering handoff

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clarity on your traffic profile and the incumbent behavior. Quick recap + proposed handoff to eng to scope the performance qualification: 

Summary of what we heard from Veridian during the call:
- Production traffic: ~50 sustained qps for the assistant endpoint, with daily peaks to ~200 qps for short windows (1-2 minutes).
- Typical request size: 120 tokens in prompt, ~40 tokens generated on average.
- Current provider observed e2e (edge-to-app → model → render) p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.2s for baseline 95% cache-hit traffic.
- Streaming: they use chunked responses for long-form summaries; client expects first chunk within 200-300ms for interactive feel.

Redwood-hosted targets we discussed:
- Target E2E SLOs for decisioning: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 600ms (hosted API, us-east region)
- Throughput targets: sustain 50 qps, burstable to 200 qps; ~8 concurrent streaming connections per instance in their topology.

Handoff asks for the engineering qualification runbook (what Ben/Jonas will own):
1) Test matrix: baseline (50 qps steady), burst window (200 qps for 90s), streaming concurrency test (8 concurrent streaming sessions * 25 clients). See attached slo_matrix.csv for full matrix.
2) Traffic shaping: replicate token distribution from call (120 in, 40 out).
3) Measurement points: client perceived TTF-first-chunk, total response time (edge ingress → first byte of final chunk), and tail p99 under cold-KV-cache conditions.
4) Acceptance criteria: Redwood-hosted must meet p95/p99 targets above in 3 of 3 runs, and demonstrate incremental fallback behavior (model-variant fallback with <5% throttled requests during burst).

Attachments: slo_matrix.csv (test cases), kpi_latency_diagram.png (measurement points), draft runbook referenced below.

Next steps: 
- Ben: schedule a 2-hour eng kickoff with Veridian SRE + our perf team — propose Monday 2026-08-31 14:00 ET.
- Jonas: prepare perf harness + a quick alpha test harness we can run in their staging by end of week.
- Alex / Veridian: confirm staging credentials and any IP allowlists for load generators.

If that aligns, I’ll open the HubSpot task and drop the Drive folder link.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---

From: Alex Pritchard <alex@veridian.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-30T18:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Veridian latency targets & engineering handoff

Thanks — this is perfect, Camila. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

1) The incumbent numbers I shared were measured from our EU region; US clients see ~10% lower latency. For parity let's use the US baseline (so incumbent p95 ~380ms / p99 ~1.08s).
2) Streaming behavior: our SDK opens ~6 long-lived connections per user session; we can simulate 8 per your matrix but prefer to start at 6 for the first run.
3) Staging constraints: staging cluster has smaller nodes (no autoscaling). We can provision a larger staging cluster for the test window but need an approved IP allowlist.

We can confirm Monday 2026-08-31 14:00 ET for the handoff. Staging creds: I’ll DM the SRE contact list and open a shared AWS role for your load generator.

Questions: 
- Can Redwood tolerate a shifted acceptance threshold for the first run (p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 700ms) while we stabilize the staging topology? If you need strict 200/600 immediately we understand but want to set expectations.
- For streaming first-chunk times, do you measure from client socket open or from request arrival at our edge? We currently measure client socket open -> first chunk.

Alex
Head of Engineering, Veridian Health

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Pritchard <alex@veridian.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-30T19:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Veridian latency targets & engineering handoff

Alex — good questions. Quick answers / confirmations from Redwood side: 

- We can accept the relaxed initial acceptance for the first staging run (p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 700ms) provided we hit the stricter targets in the subsequent run in prod-mirroring conditions. We'll flag the results as "staging-relaxed" in the runbook.
- Streaming metric: Redwood measures first-chunk from request arrival at Redwood edge (ingress). For clarity we'll publish both metrics in the test report: (A) client socket -> first chunk and (B) edge arrival -> first chunk.
- IP allowlist: fine — Ben will coordinate with SRE to provide load generator IPs and the AWS role.

Jonas — I’ll defer execution details to you. Can you post a short list of what infra we need for the staging window (instance types, load generator profile)? Aim to have that in the Drive folder by EOD.

Thanks,
Ben
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Alex Pritchard <alex@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-31T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Veridian latency targets & engineering handoff

Pulling in the perf plan here — quick notes before the kickoff: 

Planned infra for staging run (single-test window):
- 4 x c6i.8xlarge (load generators) with the load profile in slo_matrix.csv.
- 3 x g5.4xlarge inference nodes pinned to the hosted-us-east cluster (model quantized FP16 path).
- KV cache warm-up: run 10k representative prompts to warm common prefixes prior to measurement.

Test schedule (UTC):
1) Warmup (15m): KV warm-up + small ramp.
2) Baseline steady (10m): 50 qps steady.
3) Burst test (3x): 200 qps for 90s, 5m cooling.
4) Streaming concurrency: 6 concurrent long-lived connections * 25 clients for 10m.
5) Cold-cache run: baseline with cache flush to measure tail.

Metrics we’ll publish: p50/p95/p99, first-chunk median and 95th, CPU/GPU util, open connections, error/timeout rates, and tokens/sec.

Acceptance callouts: if p99 shows >10% regression vs the expected target during the burst test we’ll capture a trace and engage runbook steps: kernel fallback, reduce model size (quant 4-bit as fallback), and route 10% of traffic to incumbent variant for patient traffic.

I’ll upload the perf harness script + expected dashboard layout to the Drive folder and tag the HubSpot task. See you at 14:00 ET.

Jonas
Perf Eng
Redwood Inference
